mainTopic: Does a חצר acquire only when its owner stands next to it? The ship story of רבן גמליאל, and the difference between a find, a gift and a גט.
overview: עולא taught that a person's חצר acquires an object for him only if he is standing next to it. רבי אבא challenged this from the story of רבן גמליאל on the ship. רבן גמליאל gave away his tithes by renting out the spot where the produce lay, even though everyone was far away at sea. A scholar in סורא answered that the tithes were acquired through קנין אגב, together with the land, and not through חצר. רבא argued that רבי אבא was right to reject this answer, and the גמרא pushed back, explaining that tithes must be 'given' and that קנין אגב counts as a strong form of giving. רב פפא offered another defense of עולא: when another person is giving the item, the חצר works even from far away, and the גמרא brings a proof from the case of a gift. רב שימי challenged this from a גט, and רב פפא answered that a גט works even against her will. רב ששת בריה דרב אידי turned that answer around with a קל וחומר, so רב אשי begins a new explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ship story: the tithe for the poor goes to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that רבי אבא is quoting finishes. רבן גמליאל also gives his מעשר עני to רבי עקיבא for the poor, and rents him its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and its place is rented to him. And another tenth that I will measure out in the future is given to עקיבא בן יוסף, so that he will acquire it for the poor, and its place is rented to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ship story that רבי אבא is using against עולא. רבן גמליאל gives a second tithe, for the poor, to רבי עקיבא, and he does it the same way: by renting him the spot where the produce sits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is 'its place is rented to him.' Renting the spot makes it the receiver's own property, like his חצר. That is how the receiver acquires the produce even though he is far away on the ship. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And its place is rented to him. The spot becomes his property for acquiring.
A tenth; here the tithe for the poor (מַעֲשֵׂר עָנִי)
So that he acquires it on behalf of the poor

phrases.english: and its place is rented to him.
phrases.notes: This finishes the line just before about רבי יהושע, who was given the first tithe.

phrases.english: And another tenth that I will measure out in the future
is given to Akiva ben Yosef,
so that he will acquire it for the poor,
and its place is rented to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that רבי אבא began quoting before this section.
steps.raayaObject: Evidence against עולא's rule that a חצר acquires only when the owner stands next to it. רבי אבא quotes this ברייתא to challenge עולא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבן גמליאל and the elders on the ship

steps.title: They were not standing next to the field
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks: were רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא standing next to רבן גמליאל's field? No, they were on the ship, yet they still acquired.
steps.simpleTranslation: But were רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא standing next to רבן גמליאל's field?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא points out the problem. Everyone was on the ship, far from the field, yet the rented place still acquired the tithes for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said a חצר works only when the owner stands next to it. Here the rented spot worked as their חצר even though they were far away. So the ברייתא seems to go against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it so that…? It opens a question that expects the answer 'no'.

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence looks like a question, but it is really an attack. It means: obviously they were not standing there, so how did they acquire?

phrases.english: But were Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva
next to the field of Rabban Gamliel
standing?
phrases.notes: Of course not, they were all on the ship together.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּצַד שָׂדֵהוּ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָיוּ עוֹמְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted to attack עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that a חצר acquires only when the owner stands next to it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ship story, the rented place acquired for people who were far away. So standing next to the field should not be needed.

steps.title: עולא brushes off the question
steps.stepSummary: עולא does not answer the question. He says the questioner seems like someone who has not learned the material.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This one of the rabbis seems like people who have not learned the teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא pushes the question away without giving any answer. He treats it as not worth discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a dismissal, not a real answer. עולא gives no reason why the ship story does not disprove him, so the question is still open. That is why רבי אבא brings it up again in סורא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: עולא is talking to רבי אבא.

phrases.english: This one of the rabbis seems
like people who have not learned the teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּמֵי הַאי מֵרַבָּנַן כִּדְלָא גָּמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: עולא responds to רבי אבא's challenge by waving it away.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole challenge, waved away with no reason given
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: None is spelled out. עולא only suggests that the questioner lacks proper learning.

steps.title: רבי אבא retells the exchange in סורא
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אבא arrives in סורא, he tells the scholars there what עולא said and how he challenged him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came to סורא, he said to them: This is what עולא said, and this is how I challenged him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a transition line. רבי אבא repeats the whole argument in a new place, and this sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since עולא never really answered, the challenge was still open. Retelling it in סורא gives a different scholar the chance to answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: סורא, a major Torah center in בבל

phrases.english: When he came to Sura,
he said to them:
This is what Ulla said,
and this is how I challenged him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings back the challenge that עולא left unanswered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling here. This is a story transition that brings the open challenge to new listeners.

steps.title: A scholar answers: it worked through land, not through חצר
steps.stepSummary: A scholar in סורא answers that רבן גמליאל did not use חצר. He transferred the movable produce together with land, which is called קנין אגב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the rabbis said to him: רבן גמליאל transferred the movable items to them along with the land.
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar answers רבי אבא's challenge. He says the ship story worked through a different kind of acquiring, so it says nothing about the חצר rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting the place counts as acquiring land. Movable items can be acquired together with land, even from far away. So the ship story has nothing to do with חצר, and עולא's rule about standing next to the field still holds.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that קנין אגב is a separate way of acquiring from חצר. One case can often be explained through more than one kind of קנין.

phrases.english: One of the rabbis said to him:
Rabban Gamliel, the movable items
along with land, he transferred to them.
phrases.notes: The 'land' is the spot he rented to them, and the tithes came along with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִטַּלְטְלֵי אַגַּב מְקַרְקְעֵי הִקְנָה לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real answer to the challenge that עולא had only brushed off.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes how the source works: a different קנין was used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rented place acted as a חצר for receivers who were far away, against עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce was acquired through קנין אגב with the land, so חצר was never involved.

steps.title: רבי זירא accepts the answer, רבי אבא does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבי זירא accepted the קנין אגב answer, but רבי אבא did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא accepted it; רבי אבא did not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how the answer was received. One sage was satisfied with it, and the one who asked the challenge was not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא still thinks the ship story shows a חצר acquiring from far away, so to him the challenge against עולא stands. In the next step רבא backs רבי אבא, and step 8 pushes back on רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: עולא: a חצר acquires only when the owner stands next to it. Challenge: the ship story of רבן גמליאל. Answer: it worked through מטלטלי אגב מקרקעי. רבי זירא accepted this answer and רבי אבא rejected it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira accepted it,
Rabbi Abba did not accept it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא קַבְּלַהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לָא קַבְּלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how the sages responded to the answer in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The answer splits the sages: רבי זירא accepts it, and רבי אבא keeps his challenge.

steps.title: רבא supports רבי אבא against the transfer-with-land answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that קנין אגב cannot explain the story, because if it could work, חליפין with a cloth would have worked too. Since it didn't, the right to choose (טובת הנאה) must not be something that can be acquired.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי אבא was right not to accept that answer. If the tithes could be acquired along with land, why didn't they just use a cloth and acquire them through exchange? It must be that the benefit of choosing who gets the tithes is not real property. So it cannot be acquired through exchange, and it also cannot be acquired along with land.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the קנין אגב answer from step 5 and says רבי אבא was right to reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל did not own the tithes outright. He only had טובת הנאה, the right to choose which לוי or poor person gets them. רבא reasons that if that right were real property, the easy method of חליפין would have been used. Since it wasn't, the right is not property, so קנין אגב can't work either, and we are back to חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: He did well, he acted correctly
A cloth, used for a symbolic exchange
Acquiring through a symbolic exchange (קנין סודר)
The benefit of choosing who will receive the gift

phrases.english: Rava said:
He did well not to accept it,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אבא, who didn't accept the קנין אגב answer back in step 6.

phrases.english: for did they not have a cloth
to acquire from him through exchange?
Rather, the benefit of choosing is not property
that can be acquired from him through exchange.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה אֵינָהּ מָמוֹן
phrases.english: Here too, the benefit of choosing is not property
that can be acquired along with land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שַׁפִּיר עֲבַיד דְּלָא קַבְּלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sides with רבי אבא's rejection in step 6 and gives a reason for it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קנין אגב answer from step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If טובת הנאה could be acquired, the simpler method of חליפין would have been used. Since it wasn't, טובת הנאה is not property, and that rules out קנין אגב too.

steps.title: Tithes need real giving, so exchange fails but land works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's reasoning. Priestly gifts and tithes must be 'given', and חליפין is a buying and selling method. Movable things transferred along with land, however, count as a strong form of giving.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. For gifts to the כהנים (and tithes), the Torah writes 'giving.' Exchange is a kind of buying and selling, so it doesn't fit. Transferring movable things along with land is a strong kind of giving, so it works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבא's argument and shows a good reason why they used land and not a cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed that if land worked, a cloth should work too. The גמרא explains the difference: tithes have to be given, not traded. חליפין feels like a trade, but קנין אגב is a true giving. So the קנין אגב answer stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so, a rejection formula

phrases.english: But that is not so:
gifts of the priesthood,
phrases.notes: The same rule covers tithes for the לוי and the poor, which is our case.

phrases.english: "giving" is written about them.
Exchange is a way of buying and selling.
Movable things along with land
is a strong form of giving.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's comparison between חליפין and קנין אגב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא missed that tithes require נתינה. חליפין fails for that reason, not because טובת הנאה isn't property.
steps.whatToRemember: חליפין is like a trade, so it doesn't fit gifts that must be 'given'. קנין אגב counts as a strong giving.

steps.title: רב פפא: a gift from another person is different
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives another way to defend עולא. Even if the transfer was through חצר, when another person actively gives the item, the חצר works even though the receiver isn't standing next to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: When another person's mind is transferring the items to you, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers רבי אבא's question on עולא from step 2 in a new way, without needing קנין אגב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's rule, that you must stand next to your field, comes from a case of finding ownerless things. רב פפא says that rule doesn't apply when an owner is giving you the item. Here רבן גמליאל was the giver, so רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא didn't need to be near the field.

keyTerms.meaning: Another person's mind is transferring ownership

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
When another mind transfers them,
it is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: דַּעַת אַחֶרֶת מַקְנָה אוֹתָן שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of step 2, separate from קנין אגב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between cases: a found ownerless item versus a gift from an owner.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא's rule about standing next to the field applies to every חצר acquisition.
steps.terutzMaskana: When someone gives the item (דעת אחרת מקנה), the חצר acquires even if the receiver is far away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a key split in the laws of חצר: finding versus receiving a gift.

steps.title: Source for the distinction: the field and the running people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for רב פפא's distinction and starts with the משנה about a field acquiring a found animal. It adds רבי יוחנן's limit: this works only if the owner could run after it and catch it.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? From the משנה: 'If he saw people running after a found object...' And רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this works only if he could run after them and reach them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for רב פפא by first bringing the base case of finding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a finding case, the field acquires only if the owner could run and catch the animals. This is the strict rule for ownerless items. The next steps will compare it to a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this?

phrases.english: And from where do you say this?
As we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה אוֹתָן רָצִין אַחַר הַמְּצִיאָה כּוּ׳,
phrases.english: "If he saw them running after a found object, etc."
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: he says "my field should acquire it for me," and it does.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
This is only when he could run after them and reach them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for רב פפא's answer in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's distinction that a gift works differently.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the field, with רבי יוחנן's limit.

steps.title: Rabbi Yirmeya asks about a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether the 'run and reach' limit also applies when the animals are given as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה asked: with a gift, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks whether a gift has the same limit as a found object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the question is clear: is the 'run and catch' rule only for ownerless finds, or for every חצר acquisition?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, he raised a question

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
With a gift, how is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the limit from step 10 to a gift.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a gift also need the receiver to be able to run and catch the animals?

steps.title: A gift is acquired even if he can't catch them
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא answers that with a gift the field acquires even when the receiver could not catch the animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא accepted it from him: a gift is acquired even though he runs after them and cannot reach them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר כהנא answers רבי ירמיה's question: a gift works even without the 'run and catch' condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that a gift is easier to acquire through a חצר than a found object. The limit from step 10 does not apply here.

phrases.aramaic: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana accepted it from him:
even though he runs after them
and cannot reach them.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With a gift, the field acquires even if he cannot catch the animals.

steps.title: The reason must be that a gift from another person is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the only reason a gift is easier is that another person is giving it, which proves רב פפא's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for this? Is it not because when another person's mind transfers the items, it is different?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof and shows that the gift ruling matches רב פפא's idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference between the find and the gift is that an owner is actively giving. So the easier rule for gifts must come from דעת אחרת מקנה, and that supports רב פפא's answer for עולא.
steps.whatToRemember: A חצר acquires a gift from another person more easily than a found ownerless item. This is how רב פפא defends עולא from the story of רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Is it not because when another mind
transfers them, it is different?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא – לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּדַעַת אַחֶרֶת מַקְנָה אוֹתָן שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reason out of step 12's ruling to prove step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא's distinction is proven: when another person gives the item, the חצר works even without the strict limits of finding.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of a bill of divorce
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי asks רב פפא: a גט is also given by another person, yet עולא says the wife only acquires it through her house or courtyard if she is standing next to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי said to רב פפא: Look at a גט. Another person, the husband, is giving it to her. Yet עולא said it only works if she is standing next to her house or her courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי attacks רב פפא's distinction by pointing to a case where someone else does the giving, but the receiver still has to be standing nearby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said that when another person gives, the חצר works even when the receiver is far away. With a גט, the husband is the one giving, so by רב פפא's rule the wife should not need to be nearby. But עולא rules that she must be next to her house or courtyard, which seems to contradict רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Another mind; another person who is actively giving the item

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi said to Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי גֵּט, דְּדַעַת אַחֶרֶת – מַקְנָה אוֹתָהּ,
phrases.english: But what about a bill of divorce, where another mind transfers it to her,
phrases.notes: The "other mind" is the husband, who is the one giving her the גט.

phrases.english: and yet Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁעוֹמֶדֶת בְּצַד בֵּיתָהּ אוֹ בְּצַד חֲצֵרָהּ.
phrases.english: It works only if she is standing next to her house or next to her courtyard.
phrases.notes: This is when the husband throws the גט into her house or courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי לְרַב פָּפָּא: הֲרֵי גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 proved רב פפא's distinction from the case of a gift, רב שימי now attacks it from the case of a גט.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that when another person gives, a חצר acquires even if the receiver is not standing nearby.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט is given by another person, the husband, yet עולא still requires the wife to be standing next to her house or courtyard.

steps.title: A bill of divorce is different because it works against her will
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that a גט is a special case, since a woman can be divorced even if she does not agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גט is different, because it can be given to her even against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends his rule by saying the גט case is not a fair comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift needs the receiver to want it, but a גט works whether or not the wife agrees. Because of this difference, רב פפא says the rule for a גט does not tell us anything about the rule for a gift.

phrases.english: A bill of divorce is different,
since it can take effect against her will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שימי's challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a גט is not comparable to a gift.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גט and a gift are alike, since in both cases another person does the giving.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גט works even without the wife's consent, so its rule cannot be applied to a gift.

steps.title: A קל וחומר knocks down the 'against her will' answer
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי argues that the difference actually works the other way: if a גט still needs her nearby, a gift should need it even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת the son of רב אידי objected: Isn't this a קל וחומר? A גט works even against her will, and still she acquires it only if she is standing next to her house or courtyard, and not otherwise. A gift, which needs the receiver's agreement, should certainly need this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי rejects רב פפא's answer by turning his own difference into a קל וחומר against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט is the easier case, because it does not even need the wife's consent. If even there she must be standing nearby, then a gift, which is harder because it needs the receiver's consent, should surely need it too. So the difference רב פפא pointed to does not help him; it makes the problem worse.

keyTerms.meaning: Objected to it; raised a strong challenge
Reasoning from an easier case to a harder case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the קל וחומר supports רב פפא. It uses his own point, that a גט works against her will, to show that a gift should need the receiver nearby even more.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, objected:
But isn't it a kal vachomer?
If a bill of divorce, which works even against her will,

phrases.aramaic: אִי עוֹמֶדֶת בְּצַד בֵּיתָהּ וּבְצַד חֲצֵרָהּ – אִין,
phrases.english: if she is standing next to her house or her courtyard, yes, she acquires it;
if not, she does not.
Then a gift, which works only with the receiver's consent,
isn't it all the more so!
phrases.notes: He means a gift should surely require the receiver to be standing next to his courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: וְלָאו קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's answer in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that a גט is different because it works against her will.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט is the easier case because it needs no consent. If it still requires her to be nearby, a gift, which needs consent, should require it even more.

steps.title: רב אשי offers a new explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רב פפא's answer and introduces רב אשי, who will explain the difference between a gift and a גט another way.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. Since the earlier answer fell, the גמרא is about to bring רב אשי's new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֶלָּא shows that the answer "a גט works against her will" has been dropped. רב אשי's actual explanation comes in the text that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drop the earlier answer and take a new one

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 16 rejected רב פפא's answer, the גמרא turns to a new answer from רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinction between a gift and a גט (the details come in the following text).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between a gift and a גט is that a גט works against her will.
steps.terutzMaskana: That difference fails, so a new explanation from רב אשי is needed.
